title: The rigidification identity-action cocone is the pinched-resolution comparison
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, right-pinched mapping spaces, realization and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Work in fixed universes large enough for all displayed constructions. Let $\mathcal S$ be the infinity category of Kan complexes in the value universe, as defined in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $C$ be a small quasicategory, $a,x$ vertices, $A=\mathfrak C[C]$, and let $H:C\to\mathcal S$ be the specific coherent functor of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], with $H(z)=\operatorname{Sing}|A(a,z)|$ and enriched action given by postcomposition after the singular-realization unit. Let $\eta\in H(a)$ be the singular vertex of the identity of $A(a,a)$, and put $M_x=\operatorname{Map}^{R}_C(a,x)$. Apply $H$ to the right-pinch family $M_x\times\Delta^1\to C$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] and precompose with the constant point $\eta:*\to H(a)$. This gives an actual coherent cocone $\lambda_x:\Delta_{M_x}*\to\Delta_{M_x}H(x)$. Let $e_x:M_x\to H(x)$ be its point map, up to homotopy, under the constant-diagram equivalence of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion], specified by the $\beta$-comparison of [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification]. Thus if $\gamma_x:M_x\to U_{\mathcal S}(*,H(x))$ is the arrow family adjoint to $\lambda_x$, then $[e_x]=[\beta_{*,H(x)}]^{-1}[\gamma_x]$.

Use the cosimplicial simplicial set $Q$, coend $V(K)=|K|_Q$, natural map $p_K:V(K)\to K$, and specified map $\theta_{C,a,x}:V(M_x)\to A(a,x)$ of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. Write $u_{a,x}:A(a,x)\to\operatorname{Sing}|A(a,x)|$ for the singular-realization unit (the map taking a simplex to its characteristic continuous simplex). In the category obtained from simplicial sets by formally inverting all weak homotopy equivalences, write $[f]$ for the image of a map $f$. The following equality holds:
$$[e_x]\,[p_{M_x}]=[u_{a,x}]\,[\theta_{C,a,x}].$$
In particular, the actual point map $e_x$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The equality identifies the point map of the displayed action cocone, including all its simplicial parameters, rather than merely agreeing on vertices or connected components. It is natural under maps of $(C,a,x)$ and is unchanged by regarding the same Kan complexes and functors in a containing universe.

proof.text: Expand the concrete functor H through the enriched category A^{top}. For each n-simplex of M_x, represented by a map J^n to C, the pinched-resolution map theta_{C,a,x} sends the corresponding Q^n-summand to A(a,x). Applying H sends this enriched arrow to postcomposition on A(a,-), followed by the singular-realization unit. Evaluating that postcomposition at the singular vertex eta of the identity of A(a,a) gives, on every q in Q^n, the characteristic singular simplex of theta(q), namely u_{a,x}(theta(q)). The calculation is compatible with all coend face and degeneracy identifications, so the coend action/evaluation map b_x:V(M_x) -> H(x) is the actual simplicial composite u_{a,x} theta_{C,a,x}, not merely a map agreeing on vertices.

source.place: Section 2.2.4, opening comparison before Proposition 2.2.4.1, specialized to the identity-action summands; the explicit coend calculation is expanded here.

proof.text:
Put $X=H(a)$, $Y=H(x)$, $R=\operatorname{Map}^R_{\mathcal S}(X,Y)$, $T=\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)$, and let $h:M_x\to R$ be induced by $H$. The naturality of $j$ in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] identifies the $H$-image prism with $jh$. The composition/evaluation clause of [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification], applied to the specified point $\eta:*\to X$, therefore gives $[e_x]=[\operatorname{ev}_\eta][\alpha_{X,Y}]^{-1}[h]$ for the normalized point map of the actual action cocone. Naturality of $p$ and the counit equation of that same node give
$$[e_x][p_{M_x}]=[\operatorname{ev}_\eta][\alpha_{X,Y}]^{-1}[p_R][V(h)]=[\operatorname{ev}_\eta][E_{X,Y}][V(h)].$$
On the $Q^n$ summand indexed by $\sigma:J^n\to C$, $E_{X,Y}V(h)$ is precisely the enriched map obtained by applying the defining enriched functor for $H$ to $\mathfrak C[\sigma]$: both evaluate the enriched simplex $H\sigma$ in $\mathbf{Kan}$. Evaluation at $\eta$ is consequently the map $b_x$ calculated in Step 1. Thus the right side is $[b_x]=[u_{a,x}][\theta_{C,a,x}]$. This uses the Q-counit formula, including the maximum/prism reparametrization, rather than identifying a coend map with an unspecified point-family equivalence.

source.place: Section 2.2.4 opening enriched Q-evaluation counit formula; Kerodon 06QR and 038A specify the canonical comparison and evaluation at the chosen point.

proof.text: The weak-equivalence clauses of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution] make $p_{M_x}$ and $\theta_{C,a,x}$ invertible in the formal localization. By [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak], $u_{a,x}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for the arbitrary simplicial set $A(a,x)$. The equation from Step 2 therefore makes $[e_x]$ invertible. To detect an actual weak equivalence without assuming saturation, fix any Kan complex $Z$ in the working universe and put $P_Z(B)=\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(B,Z)$. Precomposition makes $P_Z$ an ordinary contravariant functor. The forward implication of [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence] says exactly that it sends every weak homotopy equivalence to a bijection. By the defining universal property of formal localization, it factors through that localization (contravariantly). Thus invertibility of $[e_x]$ makes $P_Z(e_x)$ a bijection. This holds for every Kan $Z$, so the converse implication of the same criterion proves that $e_x$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This supplies the needed saturation argument; it uses neither a converse of Kan Whitehead nor any cofibrancy, fibrancy, or nonemptiness assumption on $e_x$.

source.place: Agent deduction in the weak-equivalence localization from the Kan-target realization criterion; independent of the model-localization theorem because its current dependency closure returns to this item.

proof.text: Naturality follows on each Q^n summand from the naturality clauses for p and theta, from functoriality of the enriched postcomposition action and the singular-realization unit, from naturality of the right-pinch comparison, and from the natural $\alpha,\beta,E$ comparisons in [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification]. These maps commute with the coend relations, so the equality and the weak-equivalence conclusion are natural in maps of (C,a,x). Passing to a containing universe leaves the displayed simplicial sets, maps, and weak-equivalence tests unchanged, which proves the final universe-independence clause.
